text: Rain hammering the windows, a hot filter coffee and a croissant that shattered into a hundred flakes. Brew on a wet Tuesday is unbeatable.
Walked in soaked and Kabir already had my cappuccino going. Handed me a napkin for the rain before I even asked. This is why I keep returning.
Ordered during a proper downpour and the kulhad chai still reached steaming. Bag sealed tight, not a drop spilled.
Sat by the window for three hours watching the rain, cold brew in hand, plug point right under the table. Nobody rushed me out.
First monsoon morning in Bengaluru and this pink cafe gave me a dabarah of filter coffee that tasted like the city itself.
Kids arrived drenched from the auto; staff mopped the puddle without fuss and brought hot chocolate with extra marshmallows. Muffin vanished in seconds.
Rainy 8 am rush and my cappuccino was still in hand in four minutes flat. Lid on tight, no spills on the scooter.
140 rupay ki kulhad chai aur garma garam fries, baarish mein aur kya chahiye. Best cheap evening spot in Indiranagar.
Rider got held up in the rain but the cinnamon roll was still warm and the icing had not leaked anywhere. Packed very thoughtfully.
Rainy evening treat delivered: rose latte still warm, cheesecake slice sitting perfect in its box. Cosy night in, sorted.
Twelve cappuccinos and six sandwiches for the team, every cup labelled, nothing spilled despite the downpour. Flawless bulk order.
In and out in three minutes with my usual. Zoya remembered I skip the sugar. Rain or shine these folks deliver.
Geeli shoes, sasta bill, pink walls. Do ghante baithe padhai ki, kisi ne kuch nahi kaha. Paisa vasool jagah.
Pasta arrived surprisingly hot despite the storm outside, sauce still bubbling at the edges. Slightly slow but the rider kept me posted.
The kids split a strawberry shake and demolished the pasta. Staff even found us a dry table on a chaotic wet evening.
Caught in a sudden shower near 100 Feet Road, ducked into brew, and had the best masala chai of my whole trip. Hidden gem.
Baarish bahar, steady wifi andar, aur refill bhi jaldi aa gaya. Teen ghante kaam kiya, no complaints at all.
Ducked in to escape the drizzle, my coffee ready before I had even folded my umbrella. Strong, silky, done.
Iced latte arrived sealed proper, kraft bag completely dry despite the downpour outside. Still cold, not at all diluted.
They know my order before I sit down. Same great taste every single visit, rain or shine.
Monsoon evening matcha delivered to the door - arrived warm and tasted freshly whisked even after the ride across Indiranagar.
Picked up nine filter coffees and four croissants for the standup. All packed into two sturdy bags, labels right, still hot.
Rainy Sunday order for the kids: fries crisp, shake thick and cold, reached faster than the app predicted. Everyone at home happy.
Filter coffee 120, muffin 160, aur baarish dekhte hue baithne ka sukoon free. Budget mein full paisa vasool.
The cashier suggested rose milk with sabja when she heard I had never tried it. Chennai classic in a Bengaluru rainstorm. Delightful people.
Thunder outside, quiet pink cafe inside, my usual order made perfectly with real latte art. Three productive hours, zero complaints.
Thought a waffle would die in delivery. It did not. A vent in the box kept it crisp, maple packed on the side, still warm.
Meera saw me shaking off my umbrella and had a kulhad chai on its way to my usual corner before I finished drying my glasses. Home away from home.
Slow rainy morning, a perfect pour and a warm pastry while the split-flap board clacked away. Nobody hurried us at all.
Wet morning queue but the counter moved fast. Filter coffee sealed properly and still hot all the way to the office.
Baarish ho rahi thi, hum teeno ko table mil gayi, bill bhi sasta pada. Sabse sasti aur sabse cosy jagah.
Hot chocolate in this weather felt like a warm hug. Arrived hot, marshmallows intact, zero spillage in the bag.
Wet weekend, two cranky kids, and the team turned it around - a waffle to share, hot chocolates, patient smiles throughout.
Same order, same punch, teen minute mein ready even with half of Indiranagar sheltering inside. Consistent as ever.
Solid coffee, slightly longer wait than usual with everyone dodging the rain inside. Still made my bus on time.
Avocado toast travelled better than expected on a wet evening - sourdough still had bite, chilli crunch fresh. A little late but fine.
Fries aur chai hostel tak garma garam pahunche, baarish ke baawajood. 350 mein do log khush. Thoda late aaya bas.
Paneer tikka sandwich tasted great, just slightly warm rather than hot after the rainy ride. Would happily order again.
Good coffee, decent wifi even with the place full of people sheltering from the showers. Table wobbled a bit is all.
Still the best cup on the street. Prices have crept up a little this season but honestly it remains worth it.
Patient staff with the kids and the food was a hit. A bit cramped with four of us plus everyone's wet raincoats everywhere.
Ordered a cappuccino and croissant to the hotel during the rain - arrived a little late but warm and the croissant still flaky.
Fries arrived mostly crisp despite the wet ride - the box lid has vents, clever. Lost a little crunch at the bottom only.
Ten lattes and muffins for the office in the rain. One muffin came as a croissant instead, but all cups labelled and dry.
Cheese toast tight pack karke diya hostel walk ke liye. Line lambi thi baarish ki wajah se par chalti rahi. Rate bhi theek.
Rainy evening, pink glow, rose latte. Only gripe - the music ran slightly loud for conversation, though the vibe made up for it.
Managed the corner seat near a plug on a packed wet afternoon. Slightly noisy but headphones fix that. Drink was smooth too.
Four minutes for my usual shot while umbrellas jammed the doorway. Cup double-lidded, survived the scooter ride home.
Chai monsoon jitni reliable hai. Zoya akeli counter aur floor dono sambhal rahi thi aur phir bhi smile ke saath. Hats off.
Delivery took extra time in the rain but the pasta was still warm enough for the kids and the shake stayed thick. Fair portions.
Matcha whisked fresh and a cheesecake worth photographing. Slightly tricky to find in the rain - keep that pink signage lit.
Croissant travelled surprisingly well - still flaky, not squashed at all. Rain delayed the rider but the app kept me posted.
Baarish ke din 120 rupay mein filter coffee, kya chahiye. Counter thoda slow tha par bhaiya ne maafi bhi maangi. Chill jagah.
Carried eight cappuccinos back through a drizzle. Trays held, lids sealed, one cup mislabelled but everyone found theirs.
Waffle reached still crisp-edged with fresh berries on a rainy night. Rider ran a little late in the weather, worth it anyway.
Camped three hours through two rain bursts. Drinks great, snacks decent. Staff never once hinted I should leave.
Chilli cheese toast arrived warm not hot, still bubbling at the edges though. Rain tax, I understand. Tasty regardless.
Tried the rose latte on Meera's recommendation - floral without being soapy. Only gripe: my usual corner was occupied by a damp rucksack.
Hot chocolate and fries delivered for the kids on a wet evening - arrived warm, cups slightly dented but nothing spilled.
Flat white ordered in during the heaviest shower - a few minutes late, still warm, no dilution. Understandable on a day like this.
Baarish ke din ka perfect sasta combo mila. Bas seats kam padti hain jab poora Indiranagar andar aa jata hai.
Filter coffee frothed properly in the dabarah - the real deal. The server patiently explained the whole menu to a confused visitor.
Matcha latte arrived a little cooler than ideal but still good, and the cup was sealed well for a wet ride across town.
Office order of sandwiches and filter coffees mid-downpour. Every item present, just cooler than we would have liked on arrival.
Warm pastry from the oven while thunder rolled outside. Slightly squeezed at our two-seater, but the cosiness is the point.
Cappuccino has crept up in price enough to make me wince slightly, but the shot quality has not dropped. Still my daily stop.
Cappuccino achha tha jab aaya, but barah minute bheegi line mein train pakadni ho toh ideal nahi. V slow today.
Fries arrived lukewarm and soft after the rainy ride, though the peri-peri dust still tasted great. Get them fresh at the cafe.
Kulhad chai toh badhiya thi par geele bags leke fifteen minute table ke liye khade rahe. Baarish ka crowd alag hi level.
Kids' shake and pasta took over an hour on a soaked evening - tasty enough, just cool by the time it reached our door.
Flat white arrived decent but lukewarm after a slow rainy delivery. The drink itself is clearly well made at the counter.
Drinks fine as always, but a packed rainy-day cafe means chattering crowds and no plug points free. Productivity stayed limited.
Charming spot and real filter coffee, but the queue barely moved with the whole street sheltering inside. Twenty-five minutes for a coffee.
Over an hour for pasta on a rainy night - partly the app's fault honestly. Arrived warmish and tasted fine after reheating.
Bulk order for the team: croissants great, but three lattes marked wrong and one missing entirely. Wet day chaos maybe, still annoying.
Usual hamesha jaisa solid, par baarish ke crowd ne teen minute ka kaam fifteen kar diya. Pickup shelf banao regulars ke liye.
Matcha sach mein acchi hai par 290 student budget pe chubhta hai, aur rider ko rain mein aadha ghanta lag gaya.
The shake's lid was not fully sealed and the rain-soaked bag did not help - a third of it had sloshed out. What remained was tasty.
Ordered a rose latte and cheesecake in - latte arrived lovely but the cheesecake box corner was crushed in the wet ride. Mixed bag.
Rainy rush and the counter collapsed into chaos - got my cappuccino late and the lid popped off on the road. Tastes great though.
Dripping-wet crowd meant zero free tables and somebody's raincoat parked on my chair. Drink was fine; the settling-in never happened.
Kulhad chai was aromatic and lovely. But twenty minutes at the counter in a cramped rainy queue dulled the charm a bit.
Cheese toast arrived cold and the cheese had set into a slab. Flavour underneath was clearly good - delivery in rain is a gamble.
Usual order standard as always, but the new face at the counter got flustered and forgot my ticket twice. Off day in the rain.
Pre-ordered pickup for ten people still took twenty minutes in the monsoon rush, and two muffins were missing from the bag.
Fries mast the aur saste, par humein geele corner table pe baithna pada jahan AC vent tapak raha tha. Rainy day problems.
Food was worth the wait; the wait was just long - thirty-five minutes with hungry kids on a stormy evening tests anyone.
Croissant flat daba hua aaya geeli paper bag mein. Buttery toh tha, but dikha sad. Wet days ke liye better boxes chahiye.
Hot chocolate was comforting on a wet night, but 230 for a small cup with nowhere dry to sit makes it feel steep.
Counter queue out the door, one flustered cashier, and a drink that was honestly perfect once it arrived. Storm-day staffing needs work.
Cappuccino arrived cold with the foam collapsed, and the cup had leaked into the bag. Rain is no excuse for a loose lid.
Eighteen minutes for a single espresso while the counter juggled wet walk-ins and delivery pings. Missed my cab. The shot itself was decent.
Na seats, floor gila, aur portions chhote ho gaye same price pe. Baarish ne crowd la diya aur cafe cope nahi kar paya.
Kids' dinner arrived an hour late and cold, plus the shake was missing entirely. Two hungry kids and one soggy bag. Done with rainy-night orders.
Wanted to love this pink place but waited thirty minutes for filter coffee with nowhere to sit while my shoes dripped. Charming idea, poor execution.
Waffle box arrived soaked through and the waffle itself was a cold soggy disc. Maple cup had tipped over everything. A mess.
Could not work at all - every table taken by people drying off, loud chatter, my drink took twenty minutes. Left for a quieter spot.
Team lunch disaster: half the cappuccinos wrong, sandwiches cold, one bag missing a whole stack of items. Rain delay is one thing, chaos another.
Cheesecake ordered at eight, arrived at nine forty-five, half-collapsed in the box. Flavour was genuinely excellent - fix the delivery timing.
Stood in the rain-side queue forever, then found they had made me a latte instead of a flat white. Loyalty taking a hit this week.
Baarish mein ghusse toh koi table nahi, staff ne bas 'wait karo' bola. Order theek tha but service bilkul nahi.
Aadha ghanta hot chocolate aur fries ke liye, do bheege restless bachche saath mein, aur koi sukhi table nahi. Aadha chhod ke chale gaye.
Pasta arrived cold and clumped, sauce congealed, ninety minutes after ordering. For 330 rupees I expect better even in rain.
Sheltered from the downpour and ordered a cappuccino. Twenty-two minutes later, still nothing - walked back out into the rain anyway.
Ordered a rose latte to go while sightseeing in the rain. Got a plain latte after a long wait and was too wet to argue.
Eight filter coffees arrived in one sagging wet bag, three cups tipped sideways, half the items missing. Team got napkins, not breakfast.
Ordered an iced latte, received a warm cup of what tasted like sweet milk. Wrong drink, wrong temperature, wrong everything.
Twenty-five minutes for one coffee on a rainy morning and the cashier could not care less. I left without it. Never again.
Drink spilled through the whole bag, cup half empty and lukewarm, sludge over everything. Straight into the bin.
Bheegte hue andar aaye, koi seat nahi, staff rude, order toh aaya hi nahi. Worst rainy evening. Kabhi nahi aaunga.
Cappuccino tasted burnt and watery at the same time - did not know that was possible. Price went up too. This is not the brew I knew.
Whole family order arrived wrong: pasta missing, shake spilled, everything cold. Kids cried, we cooked instant noodles instead. Awful.
Rude counter, forty-minute wait, and my order was simply forgotten. Walked back into the Bengaluru rain, defeated.
Baarish ne sabko andar ghusa diya aur cafe shelter ban gaya, workspace nahi. Na plug, na table, drink bhi patli. Left quickly.
Pre-ordered fifteen cappuccinos for a client meeting. Counter had no record, remade only six, meeting started without coffee. Embarrassing.
Rainy night cheesecake order: box crushed, slice flipped upside down, glaze smeared over the lid and everything cold. Dreadful.
Sandwich box arrived crushed and wet, toast soggy, paneer filling cold and greasy. Bin, not dinner.
Pachaas minute fries ke liye, baarish mein?? Aur diya kisi aur ka cheese toast. Bilkul bakwaas service.
Escaped the storm, waited twenty minutes, watched four delivery slips jump ahead of me, left without my drink. Sort your priorities.
Three years coming here. Today: ignored at the counter, chai never arrived, walked out into the rain. Maybe my last visit.
Sunday brunch done right - the waffle arrived crisp at the edges with maple pooling in every pocket and berries actually fresh. Worth each minute.
Weekend brunch with the kids - shared one waffle then ordered a second, plus hot chocolates. Packed room but the team kept smiling.
Saturday brunch scene: cheese toast aur fries teen logon ne split kiye, bill bilkul sasta. Crowded but full vibes.
Bumped into the famous brunch crowd at this pink cafe and stayed anyway - filter coffee in a dabarah while the room hummed. Lovely chaos.
Saturday rush and they still made my usual exactly right. The place was packed and nobody's order seemed to suffer.
Brunch crowd at the door but takeaway was still five minutes. Croissant for the road, cappuccino for the drive. Efficient.
Ordered the waffle for a lazy Sunday in bed - arrived warm, maple packed on the side, berries not even bruised. Weekend made.
Came at opening, grabbed the corner before the brunch wave hit, and worked through the morning buzz. They never rushed me out.
Four of us, one crowded Saturday, zero drama. Pasta for the parents, fries for the kids, and staff found us the pushed-together table.
Brunch date at home: rose latte and strawberry cheesecake delivered - latte warm, cheesecake upright in its box. Partner took forty photos anyway.
Picked up eight sandwiches and six cold brews for a Saturday work session. Labelled, on time, every order correct despite the rush.
Sunday brunch vibe pe kulhad chai - crowd tha, energy thi, aur chai ekdum garam. Do ghante baithe full masti mein.
Chilli cheese toast delivered during peak brunch hour and it arrived still bubbling. Whatever their rider timing is, it works.
Brunch rush at brew and the staff still had time to tell me the rose milk story. Sabja seeds, chilled glass, pink everywhere. Charmed.
Avocado toast and matcha ordered in for a lazy weekend - toast still had crunch, matcha arrived warm. Slow Sunday sorted.
Kabir at the machine on a mad Saturday and my cappuccino still came with a heart on top. Cinnamon roll to share. Standard: kept.
Birthday brunch for my daughter - waffle stacked with berries, shake thick enough to need a spoon. The team made it feel special.
Weekend queue out the door but the counter line moved fast. Two minutes, perfect little shot, on my way.
Family Sunday lunch ordered in - pasta hot, hot chocolate untouched in its sealed cup, both arrived together. Rare reliability.
Hostel pe order kiya - iced latte aur peri-peri fries aaye ekdum thande aur crisp. Saara Sunday andar hi nikal gaya, no regrets.
Watched the waffle come off the griddle from our tiny table - crisp, golden, maple running into every square. Weekend ritual now.
Beat the brunch rush at opening, settled in by the window, and they let me stay even as the tables filled up. Grateful for that.
Quick takeaway amid the Saturday chaos. Counter was slammed but my order came out in minutes, exactly right. Machine-like crew.
Cheesecake delivered to my hotel after a long day out - slice perfect, glaze bright. Skipping the famous queue actually worked.
Ordered pasta home when we could not get a table - arrived hot in twenty minutes, kids approved, parents relieved. Backup plan works.
Cheese toast aur chai hostel mein manga liye - teen logon ne split kiya, sasta pada, Sunday sorted. Brunch bina crowd ke.
Cold brew and a blueberry muffin delivered for my Sunday paper ritual - cold, fresh, arrived before I had found my glasses.
Saturday brunch perfection: flat white, warm croissant, a two-seater by the window and the whole lazy morning ahead of us.
Fifteen drinks for a weekend volunteer meetup, every cup tagged by name. The brunch rush did not break their system at all.
Kids' weekend drinks ordered in - arrived warm and properly sealed. They call it 'the pink place'; even the delivery bag is stamped pink.
Rare slow Saturday for me - actually sat down instead of rushing and watched the brunch ballet behind the counter. Impressive operation.
Kids' weekend order - shake and fries arrived together, both at the right temperature. Even on their busiest day, no shortcuts taken.
Matcha delivered to my hotel mid-brunch-rush - tasted freshly whisked, arrived warm. Heard the queue was out the door; glad I ordered in.
Zoya ne pushed-together table bacha li jab hum chaar log aaye. Chai sabke liye order ki. This crew looks after its own.
Waffle and rose latte on a busy Sunday - both lovely. Only minus: a twenty-minute wait for a two-seater. Still smiling though.
Fries ne spot hit kiya brunch rush mein. Teen log thodi squeeze hokar two-seater pe baithe, but weekend hai - chalta hai.
Waffle and shake delivered for the kids' weekend treat - waffle still crisp, shake thick. Ran slightly late, the kids forgive them.
Flat white to go amid the weekend scrum - seven minutes instead of four, decent. Quality held even under the Saturday load.
Paneer tikka sandwich delivered during their peak - arrived warm, chutney still punchy, just ten minutes past the estimate.
Worked the early shift before the brunch crowd rolled in - steady wifi, calm room. By noon too loud for calls, but mornings are gold.
Saturday madness, but cup solid thi. Usual corner ek family of four ko mil gayi - unhe bhi brunch chahiye tha, no complaints.
Filter coffee and cheesecake during the weekend rush. Delicious both, though the buzzing room is more lively than relaxed.
Weekend pickup for the team breakfast - ten items, all correct, though I queued fifteen minutes behind the brunch crowd.
Cheese toast badhiya tha, mahaul Saturday ko full pada tha. Table ke liye wait karna pada but food ne compensate kar diya.
Cinnamon roll reached warm with the icing intact, even mid-brunch-rush. Deduct a little for the flattened box corner.
Avocado toast delivered for a slow Sunday - arrived neat, chilli crunch still fresh. Box slightly dented, contents perfect.
Food good, kids happy. The queue stressed the little ones a bit, but the staff kept checking on us the whole wait.
Sunday ka usual to go. Counter crowded tha but they called names in order and got mine right. Reliable even in the crush.
Group study brunch - sab kuch sahi tha, bas do logo ke liye table thodi choti padi. Weekend ka scene hai, expected.
Waffle delivered in the lunch slot - still crisp, maple on the side. Rider took a while finding the gate but the food saved the day.
Tried both the rose milk and the rose latte on a packed Saturday. Rose milk wins for me. Room was heaving but the vibes were friendly.
Weekend lunch for the kids ordered in - hot chocolate and fries warm on arrival. Delivery slow at peak hour but forgiven.
Last free plug table mil gayi noon se pehle. Weekend afternoons ambience ke liye hain, spreadsheets ke liye nahi - drink steady thi.
Saturday delivery for a workshop - all twelve items correct, sandwiches well packed. Slightly late, forgivable at that volume.
Usual order as silky as ever amid the brunch storm. Service ran a touch slower but everyone was clearly doing their best.
Grabbed a croissant for the road on a mobbed Sunday. The bag got a bit crushed at one corner but the pastry inside was unharmed.
Iced latte ghar mangaya Saturday ko - thandi, strong, perfect. Cafe ka loud music skip kar diya, price bhi same. Smart move.
Pasta arrived hot and saucy in the weekend slot. Portion felt slightly small for 330 but the taste absolutely carried it.
Rose latte on a packed Saturday, still made with obvious care. The queue to order ate ten minutes of my morning though.
No table free, so a waffle packed for a park picnic instead - stayed crisp in the box and the kids demolished it on the grass.
Masala chai and a cinnamon roll in a buzzing pink room. Crowded, cheerful, a little slow. Very Indiranagar, honestly.
Strawberry shake delivery mein bhi thick thi, weekend peak pe aadha ghanta laga aane mein. Taste ke liye worth the wait.
Cheesecake slice reached intact during peak hours - glaze perfect, base still firm. A touch late, but who minds on a Sunday.
Early drink before the brunch crowd - peaceful. Once the families rolled in it became headphone territory. Good place either way.
Split a waffle and two flat whites. Lovely morning, though watching others hover for tables adds a light guilt to the last bite.
Weekend team order: eight cappuccinos, six muffins, all present and labelled. Long queue to collect but the staff were organised.
The waffle itself was lovely, but forty minutes for a table and fifteen more for food on a Sunday tested our patience properly.
Cheese toast toh sahi tha par weekend crowd mein standing corner mein khana pada. Good food, zero seats, mixed feelings.
Pasta for the kids ordered in - arrived late and lukewarm on a packed Sunday. Tasted fine once warmed; the delay hurt hungry toddlers.
Weekend takeaway took twelve minutes instead of four. Cappuccino fine, but if I wanted to wait that long I would have sat down.
Brunch-time waffle delivery: an hour in transit, arrived warmish and slightly soft around the edges. The maple rescued it mostly.
The room becomes unusable at weekend brunch - chatter wall to wall and my calls went to voicemail. Drink was good; work, impossible.
Heard great things, but Sunday morning meant a thirty-minute queue and standing room only. The filter coffee was worth it, barely.
Usual order survived the brunch rush; my patience did not. Lost my table mid-order to a quicker group. Please sort the seating system.
Kids' order came late on a packed Sunday - drinks separated, snacks gone soft. Salvaged a rough afternoon, just barely.
Weekend bulk order arrived twenty-five minutes late with two croissants swapped for muffins. Tasty, but a client call ran coffee-free first.
Chai mast thi but do baje Sunday ko yahan aake khade raho - koi seat nahi mili. Aadha order khade hi khatam kiya.
Weekend delivery was slow and the fries softened on the ride over. Cheese toast still good. Order off-peak if you can manage.
Cheesecake ordered in on a busy Sunday - gorgeous slice, but the box arrived dented and tilted. Peak-hour service shows even in delivery.
Kids' drinks took over an hour by delivery and arrived just warm. Everyone had melted down by then. Peak-hour struggles are real.
Counter buried under brunch tickets, v chaotic. My drink was excellent when it finally appeared, twenty minutes after ordering. Weekend reality.
Took a rose latte to go when no seats freed up. Fifteen minutes for one drink; at least it was pretty and pink for the walk.
Family order at Sunday lunch: pasta great, shake half-spilled in the bag, forty minutes late overall. A properly mixed experience.
Fries crisp aur saste the but table ke liye itna wait kiya ki friends ne plan hi badal diya tha. Standing by the pastry fridge, ate anyway.
Usual order fine as always, but the Saturday scrum means no hello from the team anymore. I miss the calm weekday version of this place.
The room was a wall of brunch chatter and laptops-on-laps everywhere. Packed up after one hour. Weekdays only for me from now on.
Avocado toast ordered in on Sunday - arrived pretty but slightly soggy underneath, and the box was dented. Weekend overflow shows in delivery too.
Pre-ordered food for a Saturday event; pickup still took twenty minutes behind the brunch line. The food itself was spot on though.
Food was great once it landed on the table. Before that: thirty-five minutes standing, a crowded doorway, and hovering hopefuls everywhere.
Chai aur fries ne din bacha liya, but table ke liye itna lamba wait kiya ki poora group almost chala gaya tha.
Brunch with three kids: forty-five minutes standing, then told the waffle batter ran out. Kids cried, we left hungry. Manage the rush better.
Weekend takeaway should be faster than dine-in, not twenty minutes. The cappuccino was decent, which somehow makes the wait sadder.
Sunday lunch order arrived cold and late, pasta clumped together. Peak rush is no excuse when the order went in at noon sharp.
Waited forty minutes for cheesecake that turned out to be the last slice - dry edges, clearly sitting since morning. Overhyped place.
Sunday ko gaya, bheed itni ki chai bhi thirty minute mein aayi aur woh bhi adhuri garam. Weekend pe bilkul avoid karo.
Love this place on weekdays. Today: ignored at the counter ten minutes while groups pushed ahead, my order arrived wrong. Deeply disappointed.
Brunch crowd meant zero plugs, zero quiet, twenty minutes for a drink. Fine for a cafe date, useless for a work session. My bad, mostly.
Weekend order: waffle soggy in a steamy box, shake separated and warm, ninety minutes late. The photos online oversold this badly.
No free tables, kids' order forgotten twice. The fries finally came and were honestly great - a shame about literally everything else.
Avocado toast and matcha during brunch rush - ninety minutes late, toast soggy, matcha separated. The menu photography promised better.
Weekend bulk delivery: half the lattes arrived spilled into the carrier, order forty minutes late. Office floor smelled like coffee; the cups didn't.
Stood in a wall of weekend brunchers, espresso took twenty-five minutes, and my ticket got called under the wrong name twice. Pure chaos.
Cheese toast accha tha jab finally aaya, but chalis minute khade rehna cramped crowd mein student budget pe hurt karta hai.
Saturday order - latte leaked into the bag, croissant squashed completely flat. What stayed edible was nice. Packaging needs weekend-proofing.
Fifteen minutes for a takeaway cappuccino while the counter served delivery slips first, pls fix. Regulars get forgotten in the rush.
Rose latte delivered during peak - arrived cold, the syrup sunk at the bottom, cup lid loose in the bag. Pretty drink, poor journey.
Drove across town for the famous waffle. Forty-minute wait, then 'sold out'. Kids devastated. Put a sign up, save people the trip.
Twenty-eight minutes for a takeaway coffee on a Saturday. Counter could not find my ticket. Left empty-handed and late for plans.
Weekend order never fully arrived - missing the sandwich, fries cold and rubbery, support unhelpful. Money gone, lunch ruined.
Ek ghanta wait kiya, seat nahi mili, order garam nahi tha, aur bill pe attitude mila. Worst Sunday. Kabhi wapas nahi.
Saturday visit: regular order bhool gaye, cappuccino galat banke aayi, corner seat bhi gayi while I waited. Favourite cafe kho raha hoon.
Overrated spot. Waited in a chaotic crowd and the filter coffee came lukewarm and bitter. The pink walls cannot fix a broken queue.
Ordered pasta at 1 pm for a small birthday lunch. Arrived at 3, cold, sauce split, box dented. Party food became apology food.
No seat, no quiet inside the crowd, my order took twenty-two minutes. I pay for a workspace and got a mosh pit. Never again on weekends.
Saturday pickup for twelve people: order lost, remade half, croissants stale, filter coffee cold. Team breakfast effectively cancelled.
Cheesecake delivery promised by eight; arrived at nine-thirty crushed sideways in its box. Contacted support, got silence. Dreadful.
Kids waited an hour for their drinks by delivery - arrived separated and lukewarm. No apology via the app either. Sunday fail, total.
Takeaway fries ke liye half hour wait? Aur packet mein aadhi quantity bhi. Weekend rush ka matlab customer ko bhool jana nahi hota.
Weekend counter is a free-for-all - no queue, no order, thirty minutes of being overlooked entirely. Felt invisible in there.
Hot chocolate arrived stone cold, half spilled, on a Sunday evening. The cup looked like it had survived a flood. Refund, please.
Match night order during the final over - fries still crackling, cheese toast bubbling. Delivery beat the surge somehow.
Festival evening and the street was jammed; the cold brew arrived sealed, chilled, not a drop lost. Impressive logistics.
Came in after the match crowds spilled out. Loud, happy, and the food still came out perfect. What an evening to be in Indiranagar.
Grabbed my usual before heading home to watch the match - three minutes even with riders crowding the pickup counter.
